utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, I have something to say about the first part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is already finished. Let's go to the second part, and there will be time for you to address these issues during the Status Conference. May I first ask the Prosecution what about the actual disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, our disclosure to the accused of the supporting material is completed on Friday under Rule 66(A)(i), so we have no further -- at the moment we have no further documents to disclose to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The second point would be we are still seized with the motion of the Prosecution requesting the assignment of Defence counsel to the accused. We can't deal with this issue today because we don't yet, as mentioned beforehand, don't yet have the translation into English. From this we have two problems: The first problem is that, Dr. Seselj, unfortunately in part your handwritten 100-page document is not legible. I'm convinced that the Translation Unit will do the very best in order to find out and to translate that what is possible. But maybe we have to come back to you and to ask you one or the other question. May I ask you: There are two possibilities. We can provide you with a laptop or with a typewriter. What would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like neither a laptop nor a typewriter because I am afraid of receiving an electric shock. But I will kindly assist your translators if they have any problems in translation. If I can sacrifice my fingers and deform them in writing 100 pages in response to the Prosecution's motion, I think that the Court must ensure translators who will translate this into the official language of the Tribunal, because I am in a far worse situation than the Prosecution is as regards the writing of submissions and various documents. I have far less personnel at my disposal than the Prosecutor has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do I understand from this that you are requesting legal aid?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why legal aid? I have never met a better lawyer than I am in my whole life. I don't need legal aid. But a typist, yes, I could use that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have to decide on this. You have the offer to make use of a laptop. You have the offer to make use of a typewriter, and especially making use of a laptop will facilitate your defence because numerous documents are best accessible by laptop because you can find some documents on CD-ROM and in an easy way to find. But let me first -- I'm afraid you didn't get this document beforehand. I have to tell you that there is a guideline, a direction on the lengths of briefs and motions, and therefore -- for example, your response to the Prosecutor's motion on assignment of counsel should not have been more than ten pages or 3.000 words. These are rules that were --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What are these rules, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... May I ask the usher to give one copy of this document in the Serbian language to the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time I'm seeing this document. This was certainly not among the documents I received. But all my previous submissions - and there have been five - were half a page long. And the translators were very successful in their translation. I assured myself of that. However, my preliminary motions as to the indictment, in relation to jurisdiction and the formal defects, will also be over 100 pages long. I have already started writing this. This cannot fit onto 10 pages. In view of the seriousness of the indictment, I may have to write over 100 pages. As you can see, I am taking this job very seriously. I don't need any lawyer to hinder me in this. As far as I know, until the beginning of the trial I only have to submit my preliminary motions, unless the Prosecution continues to bombard me with these kinds of illegal requests, because the Prosecution is abusing its rights, submitting motions which it knows in advance cannot be approved. No one in the world can deny me the right to defend myself. No one can impose Defence counsel on me, as you call them. So please tell the Prosecution to submit only serious motions so that we will not waste time on motions like this one which they know in advance are unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber in its entirety will decide on the motion filed by the Prosecution and a comparative approach shows, in fact, that there can be -- there might be some merits in this request. But as mentioned, this is not the day to decide on this. It's up to you, really up to you, to make use of the technical equipment available for you, and you have to obey these rules of this Tribunal, and from this it follows that motions during this period of time have not to exceed a certain number of pages. It depends on the nature. If you feel it necessary, you can file a request to leave for additional pages. But this is the exception, not the rule. No doubt as to the fact that until now you didn't have these guidelines. All your submissions, all the 100 pages, will be taken into count when we decide on the motion filed by the Prosecution. Then the question is - and I took it already from your answers that there are no problems in the moment with the translation of the documents as far as you are concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is another problem. You adopted a decision to the fact that the additional material, the supporting material, submitted with other documents of the Prosecutor should not be translated. However, I insist that everything must be translated. I concluded on the basis of this material that there are documents that are in the Serbian language in the original. So if the Prosecutor has translated these documents into English, then I'm sure it should not be a problem to have these documents made available to me in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Serbian language. That's the easy part. Because I will consider a document as inexistent before this Tribunal if I have not received it in the Serbian language. So I consider the existent documents only the documents submitted in the Serbian language, if you want this trial to be fair and correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You have received the decision by the Trial Chamber ordering that all the relevant decisions have to be translated, and the same is true for the motions. This was the order on translation of documents filed the 6th of March, 2003. If there should be any complaints, please be concrete and demonstrate those documents where you state that you received them in a language you cannot understand that we can resolve this problem. Are there any other problems for the Status Conference? May I ask first the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. From the side of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a few to mention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few problems that I wish to discuss. As for the first part of today's hearing, Your Honour, you said that I admitted that I had received the indictment in the Serbian language, but this was something that I never actually contested, because you failed to ask that question during the last Initial Appearance. I only made a representation as to what was read out in the courtroom. I inform you that I will avail myself of the right to object as to the failure to comply with Article 20 of the Statute. Regarding the issue of visas for the members of my closest family and my friends has not yet been -- the issue has not yet been resolved. My family and my friends will never apply for a Dutch visa, especially now that the Dutch government is supporting -- is giving its support to the American genocide and aggression against the Iraqi people. The Security Council of the United Nations is required to ensure visas. If they can ensure territoriality and official stamps, then I am sure that they can provide official visas. The Dutch government cannot participate in the decision-making as to the rights of visits. This can be done only by the Tribunal, by the administration of the Detention Unit maybe, in accordance with the appropriate rules, but the Dutch government cannot play any role in this whatsoever. And I wish to inform you've of one additional matter, Your Honour. This may be uncomfortable for you, but I have to tell you that on several occasions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let us go step by step. First of all, I want to ask you to use a civilised language and not to express yourself any kind of aggression. We are seized with the case Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj, Dr. Seselj, and not with other cases. What is now about your visum or visa. I hope you have received already, if not it's on its way, the host country agreement in a language you understand. There you will not find a lot of assistance to your problem. The solution is found in international law. As to the fact that you have to enter Dutch territory and to go through Dutch territory before coming to this Tribunal - and the same is true for your relatives or visitors - it's the rule of public international law that the country has to issue the visum or visa for this special purpose. And until now during the ten years of the existence of this Tribunal, there had been no real problems with this. So I have to ask you and the members of your family to obey these rules and to apply for a visum issued by the Netherlands, being the host country for our Tribunal. There is no other possibility. But I interrupted you. You wanted to go to another issue. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to inform you, Your Honour, that in 2001 in the month of September I personally applied for a Dutch visa so that I could pay a visit to the detainees in the Scheveningen Detention Unit. This visa was officially refused to me in a letter sent by the Dutch foreign ministry in which they claimed that I constituted a danger with respect to the national security of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. By the same token, if I constitute a danger with respect to the national security to the Kingdom of the Netherlands, then all members of my family and all my close friends apparently pose the same danger. There should be no difference in respect to that in any way. To the extent that I posed a danger to the Kingdom of the Netherlands, they do too. However, if you should persist in your request, I can only conclude that at the end of this trial, at the end of these proceedings, no matter how long they take, I will not be able to receive any visitors. But I think I can stick it out, I can take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dr. Seselj, the situation is now a different one, and I can only ask you that in case members of your families or other visitors want to come and visit you, then they may apply for the necessary visa. And should there be any problem, should there be any obstacle at all, please tell this Tribunal, and I'm quite sure we will overcome these problems and you will receive the visitors, especially your family members, in this Tribunal. Until now, there has never been an unsoluble problem. So it is up to you. Please follow the rules of international law and apply for the necessary visa, or let your members of your family apply for this visa. So there shouldn't be any problem at all. Any other issues?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Concerning the issue of visa, I consider the question to be solved and closed because I know I won't be able to receive any visits until the end of the trial. I have legal advisors who will not be able to visit me either. But as I said, I consider the issue to be closed. I also made a request to the Tribunal that the sum of $438 be paid to me, that was the price of the air ticket. I paid for my travel expenses. I think that The Hague Tribunal should cover these expenses. In any case, this was a much cheaper version than the one that would have been if I had been brought here by force. You told me, Your Honour, that you will send me, you will provide me with statutory provisions regulating the uniform of the Judges, the way they dress. I have still not received any such document. My application, therefore, is still pending. I also raised the issue of having to wear a flak jacket on the way to the Tribunal. I must inform you that this time I was given a much lighter flak jacket than the one I had last time, which I consider to be some sort of privilege. However, I have to insist that I do not need any flak jacket, I do not feel exposed to any danger. If anyone is exposed to danger here, then the Judges should also wear flak jackets, because if anyone should kill me, that would not be -- that would not be a big deal. If a Judge of the Tribunal should be killed, that would constitute a big loss for the Tribunal and the United Nations. This physical torture and harassment in the form of a flak jacket should be stopped because there have never been any attacks, any assaults to the detainees on the way to the Tribunal. Never -- there have never been any dangers established in this regard. So why should I be harassed in this way? I don't understand. This is what I have so far, unless the Prosecutor has any issue to raise. And I, of course, have the right to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Coming back to the obligation to wear a Kevlar jacket, and this time a lighter one, it's a security assessment and it's therefore that all inmates of the Detention Unit when brought to the Tribunal they have to wear this Kevlar jacket. We regard it as our duty to follow the security assessment of our security personnel, and it's our duty in respect of care of supervision emanating from the fact that we are the ones issuing the warrant of arrest against you, and therefore when there is this security assessment, that we have to take care that you run no risk at all. You have to wear this Kevlar vest in your own interest, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and this is true for all the accused appearing here in this Tribunal. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have just heard an expression that I don't understand; namely "uhicenje." I know what "hapsenje" means. It means "a great excitement." As to the word "uhicenje," I don't know what it means. I think I need the assistance of an interpreter who speaks the Serbian language. Oh, oh, an arrest warrant. Now I understand. Next time you use the right word. I've just received an answer from the interpreter. You may not have heard this. It is my assumption, Your Honour, that your interpreters have the text of the documents in the Serbian language and they are now changing the exact expressions on their own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dr. Seselj, we are here in a Tribunal where we use the -- all the three variants of the same common Serbo-Croatian language, and everybody is treated equally. And I found out that you just mentioned a concrete word. In the dictionary of the standard Serbo-Croatian language, edited in 1967 in Novi Sad and Zagreb, all the words you complained about, they were equaled. This is true for the word "Opci" and "Opsti", for the word "Tocka" and "Tacka." This is true for the word Opsina and "Opstina." So you have to accept and you have to show some tolerance. Language is a tool bringing persons, bringing people together, and to make us understand each other, but we can't expect that everybody speaks the same variant or, even worse, the same dialect. In this Tribunal, for example, we have English as one of the official languages. Sometimes also for us it's difficult to understand a person speaking Irish English, French English, German English, American English, but we have to live with this in this spirit of tolerance and trying to understand each other. So therefore, nothing will be special with you when it comes to the translation and to the translation booths. You always have to be aware. And to be honest, we don't care about this, from where a person comes, be it Zagreb, Novi Sad, Belgrade, or wherever. The main point is that it's translated into a language you understand, and there should be not the slightest problem with this. So anything additional from any parties? I can see Madam Prosecutor nodding. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, may I interrupt you. Unfortunately in the moment there was no interpretation available. Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear us now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Now we can hear you. Please proceed. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to complain about the behaviour of the Prosecutor, Madam Carla Del Ponte. In Brussels on the 6th of March she spoke for the media and for the public. That is her right, and I don't deny it. But she mentioned me in a political context. She stated: "Seselj is in Scheveningen and his departure did not cause any major upheavals," and so on and so forth. She cannot fight against me by political means as long as I am in prison. That's my opinion. And you shall judge whether I am right. She should not be using my name in any kind of political context. She can prosecute me in court, but if she is going to make speeches about me for the media in a political context, then you have to make it possible for me to do likewise. Otherwise, I insist that my name not be used in the political context of public appearances by the Prosecution. And secondly, I never caused any upheavals or any trouble or unrest in Belgrade at all, so why should my departure for The Hague cause any kind of unrest when I've been trying to come to The Hague for eight years? In December 1995 I called up the Prosecution three times by phone insisting that I should come to The Hague. So why should this cause any kind of unrest in Serbia? I wanted to come here. I am grateful that my wish has been granted. So don't fight against me politically while I am manacled, in handcuffs. There is another problem as well, and it is contained in the Prosecution motion asking that Defence counsel be imposed on me. On page 8, the Prosecution says: "The accused Seselj thrives on causing scandal, conspiracy, and publicity." I have been tried for at least -- at least 50 times in my country in Serbia, always for political reasons. Never has it happened that a public prosecutor has insulted me so badly in a public document. "The accused Seselj thrives on scandal." Your Honour, I think this cannot be tolerated. And you as the Presiding Judge of Trial Chamber II should take the necessary steps to prevent this sort of thing from happening again, because if I start insulting the opposite side, I assure you that I have more talent and more success in this sort of thing than the Prosecution and they will not find it pleasant. Since I have been in prison, I have never said anything so insulting about Mrs. Del Ponte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As mentioned before, we are still seized with this motion filed by the Prosecution. We were not able to receive your answer in writing. As soon as possible and as soon as practicable, you will receive the response and the decision by the entire Trial Chamber on this issues. Finally, under Rule 65, I have to ask you mandatorily, do you have any problems with your health at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you have any complaints about the conditions in the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the Detention Unit, I have no complaints. But I insist that the Prosecution return to me a book that was confiscated while I was out walking, the 31st volume of my collected works. If the Prosecution wants to get this book, they can buy it in Belgrade, in a bookshop. I have never owned any illegal editions. All my books are available to the public. If they ask me nicely, I can lend it to them and let them read it, but I think there's no point in brutally wrenching it from me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this problem should be resolved immediately. It shouldn't -- Do you want to --

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: No. Just to specify that it's not the Prosecutor who confiscated the book. We don't know about this book. It is probably the director of the unit detention or the -- I don't know. But it's not the Prosecutor who confiscated the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. If you have any complaints about this, don't hesitate to do this in writing. This concludes today's further appearance and at the same time the Status Conference. The hearing stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: adjourned at 10.29 a.m.
